Design: notes/design_task_model_from_ft.txt (Layer A = FT taskset, Layer B =
component graph = FTs aggregated by top-level namespace, links = trigger /
sampled / join / infra, each with measured hop latency or data age).

How to read the measured links
------------------------------
  trigger  a message hop whose receiving callback continues the chain
           (publishes onward) — precedence; label = hop latency p50
           (publish → take, paired by DDS source_timestamp; clocks agree
           within 3–8 µs).
  sampled  a message hop landing on a deposit-only callback whose node reads
           the latest value from a timer/other callback (inferred state link)
           — sample-and-hold, NOT precedence; label = data age p50 at the
           moment the consumer runs.
  Big "hop" values on rarely-published topics (maps, static config) are the
  age at reception of a transient-local sample, not a latency.

Components found (r11): /sensing 33 nodes/108 F, /perception 34/89, /planning

What matches
------------
- Every arrow of the picture that CAN be active in this scenario is measured,
  with its coupling kind and its number: Sensing→{Perception, Localization},
  Localization→{Perception, Planning, Control}, Map→{Localization, Perception,
  Planning}. The picture draws them all the same; the trace says three of
  them are TRIGGER (sensing feeds perception/localization synchronously,
  sub-ms to tens of ms hops) and the localization fan-out is SAMPLED
  (consumers run on their own timers, reading a pose 20–40 ms old).
- The "big loop" of the picture is closed through the plant; here the bag
  plays the vehicle (ext:in) and the control commands end in ext:out.

What does not match / what the picture cannot show
--------------------------------------------------
- Perception→Planning and Planning→Control are silent in this run: no
  route, no initial pose → planning never publishes a trajectory. FISH shows
  this honestly (structure present, phase zero_exec, no flow); the picture
  cannot distinguish "wired" from "active". A run with an initial pose +
  goal (or AWSIM) is needed to measure the last two hops of the loop.
- Cross-cutting components the picture omits are real and measured: /system
  (diagnostics, MRM, operation mode → control at 10 Hz) and /adapi; and the
  localization→sensing feedback.
- Coupling KIND and data AGE are new information: e.g. control's inputs are
  all sampled (pose 38 ms, steering 56 ms, MRM state 198 ms) — the sample-
  and-hold structure the design brainstorm predicted (cascaded loops at
  different rates coupled by latest-value reads).
- Static inputs separate cleanly by age (vector_map 68 s, operation mode
  5 s) from live ones (tens of ms).

Layer A behind it (same session): 143 ipc-capable subs (60 ipc / 47 dds /
36 both), 11 join outputs (concatenate_data, gyro_odometer,
obstacle_pointcloud_based_validator), 62 inferred state links in 25 nodes,
3 051 message edges with per-instance hop latency (3.09M pairs, 3 046 via
rmw_take source_timestamp), 59 state edges with data age.

Caveats
-------
- State links are INFERRED (deposit-only sub → publishing F in the same
  node); verification = uprobes (notes/plan_uprobe_join_verification.txt).
- 60 s of bag at 0.5x; one scenario; no planning/control activity.
- Hop latency pairs a take with the publish nearest to its DDS
  source_timestamp (≤ 50 ms window); intra-process hops pair consumer start
  with the last publish (method recorded per edge).
